messages:
Jane (Support): FYI — customer acme-inc reports ~30k 403s in last hour after key rotation. Error in logs: "InvalidEncryptionContext: encryption context mismatch". They see failures only for requests routed through our proxy pool p-42.
Tom (Infra): ack, can you paste a sample request/headers and KMS key alias?
Jane (Support): key alias: alias/tenant-acme-enc. Sample error log: 
```
2026-02-12T18:03:10Z request_id=abc123 service=kms proxy=p-42 error=InvalidEncryptionContext decrypt failed for key=alias/tenant-acme-enc enc_ctx="{tenant_id:acme,request_id:uuid,...}"
```
Also sending the customer curl they used: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." -H "X-Redwood-Enc-Ctx: eyJ0ZW5hbnQiOiJhY21lIiwicmVxIjoiMTIzNCIsImN1c3RvbSI6eyJzb3J0IjoiZm9vIiwibG9uZ2tleSI6InZlcnkgbG9uZyBiYXNlNjQgc3RyaW5nIn19" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/respond
```
They claim nothing changed on their side. Failures started immediately after our scheduled key rotation window.
Alice (SRE): interesting — invalid enc ctx only when proxied through p-42. Other pools fine. Could be header truncation or mutation in proxy. How big is that base64 string?
Jane (Support): customer says enc ctx base64 length ~5120 bytes (long tenant metadata).
Ben (Security): note: AWS KMS decrypt checks exact map equality for encryption context. If header truncated or whitespace changed, decrypt fails. Also rotations shouldn't affect enc ctx matching unless some shim changed how we forward headers.
Tom (Infra): checking p-42 nginx logs now. Quick grep shows a bunch of 431 status codes earlier during the rotation window (Request Header Fields Too Large). That points to header size bounds. Our ALB -> nginx pipeline: ALB forwards to nginx upstream. ALB has 8KB header limit for single header combined? Need to confirm.
Alice (SRE): reproduced locally by sending a 5KB X-Redwood-Enc-Ctx header through p-42 config: nginx truncated header (it accepts but clips at buffer size) and append behavior removed trailing bytes. KMS sees truncated JSON -> InvalidEncryptionContext.
Jane (Support): customer also reported a small billing spike from retries/recoverable errors. They're upset. They've opened a support ticket asking for root cause and mitigation.
Tom (Infra): root cause summary: after we rolled the new proxy version that added `X-Forwarded-Info` appends, some requests grew > buffer and nginx (default large_client_header_buffers) started truncating the long encryption-context header. KMS decrypt expects full map -> 403s. Rotation coincided with deploy that changed header composition, so timeline matched.
Ben (Security): next steps? This is both reliability and compliance (audit logs show failed decrypts for tenant data). We need quick mitigation and a medium-term fix.
Alice (SRE): Mitigation options (fast):
- Roll back proxy change that appends large header (p-42) — low risk, immediate.
- Strip X-Redwood-Enc-Ctx from requests to KMS proxy and send enc ctx in request body to our backend service (but KMS decrypt still needs the context) — not feasible short-term.
- Increase nginx buffer: `large_client_header_buffers 8 16k;` — must be rolled to all p-42 instances, careful with memory.
Tom (Infra): rollback is easiest. I'll queue a rollback to p-42 now and monitor 403s.
Jane (Support): told customer we're rolling back and will monitor; they appreciate the update.
Alice (SRE): medium term fixes:
- Change how we encode encryption context: compact keys and compress before base64 (saves ~60%).
- Move to a signed token referencing a server-side persisted context (store small token in header instead of full JSON).
- Add request validation at the proxy to reject/short-circuit clearly too-large enc ctx with 4xx to avoid KMS try.
Ben (Security): agree on short+medium plan. Also need to update runbook and compliance notes: failed decrypts count and explain no plaintext exposure, just failed attempts.
Tom (Infra): rollback completed at 18:19 UTC. Rolling window metrics: 403s dropped from ~600/min to ~2/min in 5 minutes.
Jane (Support): customer confirmed errors subsided. They're asking for timeline and permanent fix ETA.
Alice (SRE): ETA: compact-encoding patch + tests -> 3d. Signed-token design -> 2w (requires small persisted store, migration planning). I'll open PRs and RFCs.
Ben (Security): please capture audit artifacts: list of affected requests, timestamps, and key aliases used. We need that for compliance review. Jane, can you pull customer-facing timeline and attach to ticket?
Jane (Support): on it. I'll attach rollback time, symptom window, and mitigation plan.
KMS Proxy Bot: Automated note: p-42 rollback deployed by infra at 2623571159, health checks passing.
Alice (SRE): follow-up action items:
- Tom: run a job to scan other proxy pools for header growth risks (1d).
- Alice: open PR for compact encoding (3d).
- Ben: prepare audit summary for compliance (48h).
- Jane: update customer ticket with timeline and next steps (today).
Tom (Infra): started scan job. Found 2 other pools with potential header growth (p-17, p-88). Will schedule configuration adjustments.
Jane (Support): customer replied: "thank you — we need permanent fix as we sometimes include long tenant metadata. Will join design sync." :thumbsup:
Alice (SRE): good. I'll invite customer to design sync next Tue. Closing thread for immediate incident, keeping follow-ups in ticket #4728.
Ben (Security): marking incident P2 for compliance follow-up.
Jane (Support): closing here, moving details to ticket. Thanks team :heart:
